323109.title: Acyclic Edge Coloring Conjecture
323109.statement:
In a finite, simple, undirected graph $G$, let $\Delta(G)$ denote its maximum degree. The **acyclic chromatic index** $\chi'_a(G)$ is the least number of colors in a proper edge coloring of $G$ such that the union of any two color classes is a forest. **Acyclic Edge Coloring Conjecture.** For every graph $G$, 

$$
\chi'_a(G)\leq \Delta(G)+2.
$$

This conjecture proposes a linear upper bound for the acyclic chromatic index, improving the previously known general bounds proportional to $\Delta(G)$.

324533.title: The total 1-2 Conjecture
324533.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph. A total $k$-weighting assigns weights from $\{1,\ldots,k\}$ to every vertex and edge, and $\chi_\Sigma^t(G)$ is the least $k$ for which some such weighting properly colours adjacent vertices by the sums of the weight at the vertex and the weights on its incident edges.

**Total 1-2 Conjecture.** For every graph $G$,

$$
\chi_\Sigma^t(G)\leq 2.
$$

The conjecture is a total-weighting analogue of the 1-2-3 Conjecture. The source records the best general bound as $\chi_\Sigma^t(G)\leq 3$, so the conjecture remains open.

324536.title: Czerwiński–Grytczuk–Żelazny's additive colouring conjecture
324536.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, let $\chi(G)$ be its chromatic number, and let $\chi_\Sigma^v(G)$ be the least $k$ for which a vertex weighting from $\{1,\ldots,k\}$ properly colours adjacent vertices by the sums of the weights on their neighbours.

**Czerwiński–Grytczuk–Żelazny's conjecture.** For every graph $G$,

$$
\chi_\Sigma^v(G)\leq \chi(G).
$$

This asks whether the additive colouring number is always bounded by the ordinary chromatic number. The source presents it as open, with partial results for trees and bipartite planar graphs in the list-setting discussion.

328966.title: The acyclic chromatic index conjecture
328966.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph. Its **acyclic chromatic index** $a'(G)$ is the least number of colors in a proper edge coloring of $G$ with no bichromatic cycles, and let $\Delta(G)$ denote its maximum degree.

**Acyclic chromatic index conjecture.** For every graph $G$,

$$
a'(G) \leq \Delta(G)+2.
$$

The conjecture proposes a sharp linear upper bound for acyclic edge colorings, improving the previously known linear bound while matching the natural lower bound up to an additive constant. Its resolution status is not established by the supplied source context.

329573.title: The chromatic upper-bound conjecture for Euclidean dimension of graphs
329573.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph. Its **Euclidean dimension**, denoted $dim(G)$, is the minimum dimension of a Euclidean space in which $G$ can be represented with adjacent vertices at unit distance. Let $\chi(G)$ be the chromatic number of $G$, the minimum number of colors needed to assign colors to the vertices so that adjacent vertices receive different colors. **Chromatic upper-bound conjecture.** For every graph $G$, we have

$$
dim(G)\le 2\chi(G).
$$

This proposes a chromatic-number upper bound for the Euclidean dimension of graphs, improving on the general estimate discussed in the paper. Its resolution is not established in the supplied text.

330309.title: The equitable total coloring conjecture
330309.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite undirected graph without loops or multiple edges. An **equitable total coloring** is a total coloring in which the cardinalities of any two color classes differ by at most one. The equitable total chromatic number $chi”_{=}(G)$ is the least number of colors in an equitable total coloring, and $Delta(G)$ denotes the maximum degree of $G$.

**Equitable total coloring conjecture.** For every graph $G$,

$$
\Delta(G)+1 \leq \chi”_{=}(G) \leq \Delta(G)+2.
$$

The conjecture was proved for cubic graphs, so every cubic graph has an equitable total coloring with five colors. Its general status is not resolved in the supplied text.

330517.title: Brualdi and Massey's incidence coloring conjecture
330517.statement:
An **incidence** in a graph $G$ is a pair $(v,e)$ where $v$ is a vertex of $G$ and $e$ is an edge of $G$ incident to $v$; two incidences are adjacent if they share a vertex, share an edge, or one consists of an endpoint and the other incidence's edge. The **incidence chromatic number** $chi_i(G)$ is the minimum number of colors in a coloring of the incidences of $G$ such that adjacent incidences receive distinct colors. Write $Delta(G)$ for the maximum degree of $G$. **Brualdi and Massey's incidence coloring conjecture.** For every graph $G$, 
$$
chi_i(G) leq Delta(G) + 2.
$$
 Brualdi and Massey proved the weaker bound $chi_i(G) leq 2Delta(G)$. The conjecture is false in general: Guiduli observed that Paley graphs are counterexamples, although the bound holds for many graph classes, including cubic graphs, partial $2$-trees, and powers of cycles with finitely many exceptions.

330625.title: The ker–diadem inequality for graphs
330625.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph. Write $\ker(G)$ for the intersection of all critical independent sets, and let $\operatorname{diadem}(G)$ be the union of all critical independent sets. Let $\alpha(G)$ denote the independence number of $G$.

**Ker–diadem inequality.** The inequality

$$
|\ker(G)|+|\operatorname{diadem}(G)|\leq 2\alpha(G)
$$

is true for every graph $G$.

Together with the general inequality $2\alpha(G)\leq|\operatorname{core}(G)|+|\operatorname{corona}(G)|$, this would give a chain of inequalities relating the intersections and unions of critical and maximum independent sets. The source gives no resolution of this conjecture.

331997.title: The strong geometric description conjecture for non-parallelizable tensegrities
331997.statement: Let $G$ be a graph and let $G(P)$ be a framework whose vertex configuration $P$ is in general position. A **system of strong geometric conditions** is a system of algebraic geometric conditions on $P$ of the type defined in the paper. **Strong geometric description conjecture.** For every graph $G$ there exists a system of strong geometric conditions such that a framework $G(P)$ in general position admits a non-parallelizable tensegrity if and only if $P$ satisfies this system of strong geometric conditions. This conjecture gives an algebraic description of the configurations supporting non-parallelizable tensegrities, extending the modified form of Conjecture 2 of DKS mentioned by the authors; its resolution is not established in the supplied text.

333481.title: The narrowness conjecture for $H$-free graphs
333481.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph. A function $f:V(G)\to[0,1]$ is **good** if, for every perfect induced subgraph $P$ of $G$,

$$
\sum_{v\in V(P)} f(v)\leq 1.
$$

For $\alpha\geq 1$, the graph $G$ is **$\alpha$-narrow** if, for every good function $f$,

$$
\sum_{v\in V(G)} f(v)^\alpha\leq 1.
$$

**Narrowness conjecture.** For every graph $H$, there exists a constant $\alpha(H)\geq 1$ such that every $H$-free graph $G$ is $\alpha(H)$-narrow.

Fox showed that this conjecture is equivalent to the Erdős–Hajnal conjecture. It is known for some classes, including bull-free graphs, but remains open for general $H$-free graphs.

333717.title: Bouchard–Hertz–Desaulniers deficiency bound for graphs
333717.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, let $V(G)$ denote its vertex set, and let $def(G)$ denote its deficiency.

**Bouchard–Hertz–Desaulniers conjecture.** For every graph $G$,

$$
def(G)\leq \vert V(G)\vert.
$$

The conjecture is still open, but it holds for regular graphs, some bipartite graphs, and outerplanar graphs. If true, it would imply upper bounds for the deficiency of triangle-free graphs and of graphs with at least three vertices.

334658.title: Petrosyan–Mkhitaryan conjecture on cyclic interval colorings
334658.statement:
Let $\mathfrak{N}_c$ be the class of multigraphs admitting a cyclic interval coloring, and let $W_c(G)$ denote the maximum number of colors in a cyclic interval coloring of $G$. **Petrosyan–Mkhitaryan conjecture.**

(i) For every triangle-free graph $G\in\mathfrak{N}_c$,

$$
W_c(G)\leq \lvert V(G)\rvert.
$$

(ii) For every graph $G\in\mathfrak{N}_c$ with at least two vertices,

$$
W_c(G)\leq 2\lvert V(G)\rvert-3.
$$

The paper states that the first bound is known for graphs of maximum degree at most $4$, while the general assertions are presented as conjectures; the second bound extends the corresponding general upper-bound question beyond triangle-free graphs.

335703.title: The bounded geodecity conjecture for subdivisions of graphs
335703.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph. A **subdivision** of $G$ is a graph obtained by replacing edges of $G$ with paths. For each positive integer $m$, let $\H_m$ denote the class of graphs whose geodecity is at most $m$.

**Bounded geodecity conjecture.** For every graph $G$ there exists an integer $m$ such that every subdivision of $G$ lies in $\H_m$.

This statement is presented as a consequence of a possible qualitative converse to the result that graphs in $\H_k$ exclude $K_{2,k+2}$ as a minor. The paper does not establish it, so its status remains open.

344558.title: Akiyama's linear arboricity conjecture
344558.statement:
For a graph $G$, a **linear forest** is a forest whose components are paths, and the **linear arboricity** $la(G)$ is the minimum number of disjoint linear forests whose union contains all edges of $G$. Let $\Delta$ be the maximum degree of $G$.

**Akiyama's linear arboricity conjecture.** For every graph $G$ of maximum degree $\Delta$,

$$
la(G)\leq \left\lceil\frac{\Delta+1}{2}\right\rceil.
$$

The conjecture was raised by Akiyama and collaborators and is presented in the paper as a central related problem. The supplied text gives no resolution status.

352331.title: ZFC realization conjecture for Ext-graphs of abelian groups
352331.statement:
Let $(S,R)$ be a graph, meaning that $R\subseteq S\times S$. An **Ext-graph** of a family of abelian groups $(\mathbb G_s:s\in S)$ is the graph on vertex set $S$ whose relation is determined by vanishing of the Ext groups, namely $sRt$ exactly when $\operatorname{Ext}(\mathbb G_s,\mathbb G_t)=0$. **Ext-graph realization conjecture.** Every graph can be realized as the Ext-graph of a family of abelian groups; equivalently, for every graph $(S,R)$ there are abelian groups $(\mathbb G_s:s\in S)$ such that

$$
\operatorname{Ext}(\mathbb G_s,\mathbb G_t)=0\iff sRt.
$$

The preceding theorem establishes this consistently under GCH after passing to a cardinal-preserving generic extension, while the conjecture asserts that the positive answer to Herden's question already holds in ZFC.

358956.title: The characterization of $\mathbf{W_2}$ graphs by neighborhood independence
358956.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, let $V(G)$ denote its vertex set, let $N(v)$ and $N[v]$ denote the open and closed neighborhoods of a vertex $v$, let $N(S)$ denote the neighborhood of a vertex set $S$, and let $\alpha$ denote the independence number. The class $\mathbf{W_2}$ is the class of graphs whose independent sets can be extended to independent sets of maximum cardinality in the relevant induced subgraphs.

**$\mathbf{W_2}$ characterization conjecture.** For every graph $G$, the following assertions are equivalent:

1. $G$ is in the class $\mathbf{W_2}$.
2. $\alpha(N(v) \setminus N(S)) = 1$ for every vertex $v \in V(G)$ and for every maximal independent set $S$ of $V(G) \setminus N[v]$.

The equivalence is proved in the source for well-covered graphs; the conjecture asks whether the same characterization holds for arbitrary graphs.

366150.title: Burris–Schelp conjecture on the vertex-distinguishing chromatic index
366150.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph with at most one isolated vertex and no isolated edge. For each degree $d$, let $n_d$ be the number of vertices of degree $d$, and define

$$
\pi(G)=\min\left\{k\in\mathbb{N}\mathrel{\middle|}\binom{k}{d}\ge n_d\text{ for all }\delta(G)\le d\le\Delta(G)\right\}.
$$

Here $\delta(G)$ and $\Delta(G)$ denote the minimum and maximum degrees of $G$, respectively, and $\chi'_{vd}(G)$ is the least number of colors in a vertex-distinguishing proper edge coloring of $G$.

**Burris–Schelp conjecture.**

$$
\chi'_{vd}(G)\in\{\pi(G),\pi(G)+1\}.
$$

The quantity $\pi(G)$ is a counting lower bound: vertices of degree $d$ must receive distinct $d$-element sets of incident colors. The conjecture predicts that this bound determines the vertex-distinguishing chromatic index up to an additive one for every graph satisfying the stated necessary conditions.

368238.title: The 1-2 Conjecture for total multiset-labellings
368238.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph. A total $k$-labelling is a map $\ell:V(G)\cup E(G)\to\{1,\dots,k\}$. For each vertex $u$, let $\mu_\ell(u)$ be the multiset of labels incident to $u$, including the label of $u$. The labelling is multiset-proper when adjacent vertices have distinct incident multisets, and $\chi^t_{\rm M}(G)$ is the least $k$ for which such a total labelling exists. **The 1-2 Conjecture (multiset version).** For every graph $G$,

$$
\chi^t_{\rm M}(G)\leq 2.
$$

The paper introduces this multiset variant formally and presents it as the easiest of the three total variants; its status is open.

370752.title: The strong-product infinity conjecture for distance packing domination
370752.statement:
Let $G$ and $H$ be graphs, and let $d$ and $p$ be integers. The $d$-distance $p$-packing domination number $\gamma_d^p(G)$ is the cardinality of a smallest set of vertices that is both a $d$-distance dominating set and a $p$-packing; if no such set exists, it is defined to be infinity. The **strong product** $G\boxtimes H$ has vertex set $V(G)\times V(H)$, with adjacency inherited from adjacency in either factor or both factors.

**Strong-product infinity conjecture.** If

$$
\gamma_d^p(G)=\infty,
$$

then

$$
\gamma_d^p(G\boxtimes H)=\infty
$$

for every graph $H$.

The conjecture asks whether the nonexistence of a $d$-distance $p$-packing dominating set in one factor necessarily persists after taking its strong product with any graph. The paper establishes the upper bound $\gamma_d^p(G\boxtimes H)\leq \gamma_d^p(G)\gamma_d^p(H)$ when the relevant quantities are finite, but the converse implication concerning infinity is left as a conjecture.

371290.title: Quasi-majority neighbor sum distinguishing conjecture
371290.statement:
Let $G$ be a nice graph, meaning that it has no $K_2$ component, and let $\chi_{\sum}^{QM}(G)$ denote its quasi-majority neighbor sum distinguishing index. **Quasi-majority neighbor sum distinguishing conjecture.** Every nice graph $G\neq C_5$ satisfies

$$
\chi_{\sum}^{QM}(G)\leq 4.
$$

The paper proves that 12 colors suffice for every graph and reports that $C_5$ has the highest known quasi-majority neighbor sum distinguishing index, namely 5; whether an infinite family has index at least 5 remains open.
